player_intro: (DeckTech handle '''choker''') posted a [[Light]] [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] list on DeckTech in August 2001.

starting.card: Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers

description: One of the most solid light side decks out there right now.  Matches up great against some of the more popular dark side decks like hunt down and BHBM.
cards: Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers
posted: Wise Advice/Do Or Do Not
shields_note: The post names no Defensive Shields.
notes: Format Premiere - Coruscant: the strategy calls the deck post-Coruscant ('With the release of Coruscant the deck becomes only more powerful'); the list itself has no Coruscant-set cards.

Starting cards as posted under START (8): Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers, the Hidden Base indicator system ('[Indicator]'), Rendezvous Point, Podrace Prep, Tatooine: Podrace Arena, Boonta Eve Podrace, Anakin's Podracer and Do, Or Do Not & •Wise Advice; these count toward the 60.

Posted '[Indicator]' is the face-down planet system the Objective places from outside the deck to mark the 'Hidden Base'; the post does not name the system, so it is printed as written and counted (the published sections total 60 with it).
'PURPLE (1)' is a section header for the purple Epic Event I Did It!, not a card.

Posted 'Wise Advice/Do Or Do Not' dested the Reflections II combo Effect Do, Or Do Not & •Wise Advice; 'Ani's Saber' Anakin's Lightsaber; 'Ani's Pod' Anakin's Podracer; 'Jedi Luke' Luke Skywalker, Jedi Knight; 'Lando in Falcon' Lando In Millennium Falcon; 'Boussh' Boushh; 'Rendevous Point' Rendezvous Point.

Posted 'Out of Nowhere/Ghhhk' dested the Light combo Houjix & Out Of Nowhere (Ghhhk is the Dark counterpart of Houjix; the post uses '/' for combo cards); 'Transmission Terminated/OOC' Out Of Commission & Transmission Terminated.
Kiffex and Endor dested to the Light pages Kiffex (Jabba's Palace) and Endor (Light).
The post is signed 'Michael "the Spider Monkey" Sorrell'.
